migrations.buyerSteps: Apply after 0075, and bind INSTALLATION_KEY before the updated Worker starts: rer deploy generates it once and keeps it, and the platform provisions it on an RER Managed installation. Adds keys_sealed (default 0) and key_ids (default []) to rer_dependency_installation; the sector ID, provider links and dependency signing keys stay as they are. With the key bound, each provider signing key that rer 0.2.76 stored in plaintext is sealed at rest on first use under the same public key, so a linked identity provider keeps verifying Lamp. Without the key, dependency discovery and provider linking answer 503 installation_key_missing, and so does sign-in once an Auth provider is linked; nothing is rewritten. Archives carry the sealed keys but never the key: keep INSTALLATION_KEY with the deployment's private secrets and supply the same key when restoring into a new installation.

agentUpdateInstructions: From v1.11.2: back up data and owner source first, update the checkout, run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile (the checkout now pins @runeditrun/rer 0.2.98 and carries no rer patch) and rer deploy with the same environment and input file; the deploy applies migration 0076. An installation on v1.11.1 or earlier first honors the retained records in release-history/ through 1.11.2.json, and the same deploy applies their migrations in order. From rer 0.2.77 Base seals the dependency signing keys at rest under INSTALLATION_KEY, a generated 64-character lowercase hex Worker secret declared beside SESSION_SECRET in rer-setup.json, hosted-check.json, hosted-check-managed.json, deploy.json and both packaging declarations, with an optional INSTALLATION_KEY_PREVIOUS. rer deploy generates the key once and keeps it in .rer/deploy/<environment>.secrets.env. Lamp's deploy pipeline refuses a missing or malformed key before uploading anything, sends the key only to a Worker without one and keeps the key a Worker already holds on every redeploy; it never replaces it (LAMP_REPLACE_SECRETS does not take it) and never uploads INSTALLATION_KEY_PREVIOUS, which only rer's rotation (rer deploy --rotate-secret INSTALLATION_KEY) binds. There is no default key, so this release is breaking where a deploy binds none: dependency discovery and linking answer 503 installation_key_missing, and so does sign-in once an Auth provider is linked. An RER Managed installation must have INSTALLATION_KEY provisioned by the platform before it takes this release, and restoring an archive into a new installation needs the same key. Preserve the INSTALLATION_KEY and INSTALLATION_KEY_PREVIOUS pass-through to createDependencies and AuthConfig in src/core/platform/auth/ in any customization, preserve every published release record and immutable contract snapshot, and run the existing verifier and release validator before adopting.
